button.intent: A control that performs an action. Every button in this product is a NES.css button — the library already decided what a button is, and it decided well.
button.namespaceNote: NES.css shares `is-*` modifiers across components, so `root` narrows the check to elements that actually are buttons. Without it, `.nes-container.is-dark` would report as a button with an unknown variant.

default.intent: The ordinary action. Most of the HUD is these.

primary.intent: The action a screen is for: start the race, confirm the purchase.

confirm.intent: Completing something already in progress — repairs done, opponent recruited.

caution.intent: An action with a cost the player should notice before pressing.

panel.intent: A framed region of the HUD.

plain.intent: The library's container, unmodified. Used wherever a panel is a dialogue rather than part of the HUD grid.

hud.intent: A panel that sits flush in the HUD grid.
hud.diverges: NES.css centres a container's title over its border, which is right for a dialogue and wrong inside a grid — the overhang breaks alignment with the panel beside it. This override lays the panel out as a flex column with the system's own spacing and drops the overhang. Everything else, including the pixel border, stays the library's.

stat.intent: A labelled counter. The credits, the clock, the pedestrian tally — the HUD is mostly these.
stat.namespaceNote: No NES.css classes appear here at all, because there is no NES.css component to name. A composition's namespace is entirely the product's.

default.intent: A number with a name above it, sized so the number reads at a glance from a driving position.

parts.cm-stat__label: What is being counted. Small, muted, uppercase tracking.
parts.cm-stat__value: The number itself, in the heading colour.

critical.intent: The same counter when its number is bad news — time nearly out, damage nearly total.
critical.notes: A modifier rather than a second pattern: same component, different state. Recording it as its own pattern would have made the vocabulary look wider than it is.

driver.intent: One opponent: who they are and how wrecked. NES.css has avatars and it has progress bars; it has no notion of the two together meaning one entity.

default.intent: An opponent in the pre-race list.
default.example:
Die Anna

Hawk R — 2nd

selected.intent: The opponent the player has picked to hunt.
selected.example:
Max Damage

Eagle R — 1st
selected.notes: Uses the `selected` role, not `action`. Layer 2 draws that distinction and most products collapse it: this is a state the player is in, not an invitation to click.

damage.intent: A labelled meter with its reading beside it. Built ON the library's progress bar rather than replacing it.

parts.cm-damage__value: The reading, as text, for anyone who cannot judge a bar.

meter.example: CHASSIS72%
meter.notes: The bar itself stays `.nes-progress`, so the pixel styling and the three browser-specific pseudo-elements remain the library's problem. The composition adds only the label and the readout.

bare.intent: The library's progress bar with no label, for places where the surrounding text already says what it measures.

field.intent: A form control and its label. Untouched — NES.css already decided these and the adapter re-pointed their colours.

select.intent: A choice from a known list.
